text.content: Students add a Loop Node to the Meridian Agentflow v2 to handle HTTP failures with automatic retry logic and a controlled exit path.

text.content: Meridian's HTTP Node on Path B currently handles one response (success or failure). When the engagement status API is temporarily unavailable, Agent Node B returns a fallback message and the consultant has to try again manually. For a tool used frequently throughout the working day, that is friction the development team wants to eliminate.

rich_text.plain_text: Meridian's HTTP Node on Path B currently handles one response (success or failure). When the engagement status API is temporarily unavailable, Agent Node B returns a fallback message and the consultant has to try again manually. For a tool used frequently throughout the working day, that is friction the development team wants to eliminate.

text.content: The solution is retry logic by automatically re-attempting the HTTP call a defined number of times before falling back. The Loop Node enables the creation of cycles or iterative retries within a workflow. When execution reaches the Loop Node, it redirects back to a specified target node that has already been executed earlier in the current run, causing its re-execution along with any subsequent nodes in that part of the flow.

text.content: The Loop Node adds resilience to Meridian's canvas by handling transient failures automatically. The key design principle is that the Loop Node provides the backward redirect, but the Condition Node provides the exit. Every loop needs both.
